title: FHFA House Price Index — Monthly Index (July 2027), 9:00 a.m. ET
source: FHFA: two FHFA primaries fetched direct 2026-09-06 by this session, independently of the sweep that proposed this id. (1) fhfa.gov/data/hpi (HTTP 200, 89,663 bytes) — its "2027 HPI Release Dates" table reads "Tuesday, September 28 | Monthly Index | July 2027", the ninth of twelve dated 2027 rows (Jan 26 -> Dec 28, every one a last Tuesday, quarterly editions on Feb 23 / May 25 / Aug 31 / Nov 30, so this row is a MONTHLY index). (2) The published 2026Q2 report (HTTP 200, 1,522,949 bytes, released 2026-08-25), whose "FHFA HPI Release Dates for 2027" appendix page carries the identical row above the statement "Public FHFA HPI(R) releases occur at 9AM ET and include a press release, tables, figures, and associated data" — a published document, not a second reading of the same web table, and the source of the 9:00 a.m. ET time. Both were text-extracted in-session (the PDF's 511 content streams inflated with node zlib; this runner has no pdftotext, openpyxl or numpy). Promoted estimate -> confirmed on the precedent construction-spending-2026-12-01, new-home-sales-2026-11-25, fhfa-hpi-2026-11-24, fhfa-hpi-2026-12-29, fhfa-hpi-2027-01-26, fhfa-hpi-2027-02-23 and fhfa-hpi-2027-08-31 set: the no-self-confirm limit binds the DISCOVERING sweep (consumer-confidence-2027-09-28), not this event's own independent second look. 2027-09-28 is the fourth and last Tuesday of September 2027, consistent with the rule the other eleven rows follow. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: PROPOSED by the consumer-confidence-2027-09-28 initial-research sweep (2026-09-06) and researched the same day; the proposal file is now shadowed by this canonical one. INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-06 (docs/research/events/fhfa-hpi-2027-09-28.md) SETTLES A CONFOUND FIVE SIBLING LEDGERS EACH RECORDED AS AN UNRESOLVABLE LIMIT, AND UPGRADES THE CHAIN'S CONTROL. THE CO-OCCURRENCE IS AN IDENTITY, NOT A FEATURE OF ANY DATE: the Conference Board publishes Consumer Confidence at 10:00 ET "on the last Tuesday of every month" (conference-board.org, HTTP 200, 332,031 bytes, re-read this session) and FHFA has published on the last Tuesday 67 of 67 listed releases since 2021, so 100% of post-policy FHFA release mornings ALSO carry a CB print one hour later -- against 50 of 154 (32.5%) in the pre-policy monthly era and 1 of 50 in the quarterly era. The proposer called this pairing "the second instance of it in 2027"; it is all twelve, every year since 2021, and it means no daily bar of ANY modern FHFA release day can attribute anything to FHFA. THE CONFOUND WAS THEN REMOVED RATHER THAN RESTATED: the 104 pre-policy releases that did NOT fall on a last Tuesday are the only CB-free FHFA release days that exist, and they are null on all four metrics (n=103 with VIX; p=0.5433 / 0.2744 / 0.9605 / 0.6291), as are the 50 co-occurring ones (0.4861 / 0.3474 / 0.1019 / 0.9870). The chain's stand-aside now rests on a clean sample for the first time. THE ONE SUB-0.05 RELEASE READING IS A LATE-SEPTEMBER EFFECT, MEASURED AND ATTRIBUTED: September release days (n=5) show VIX9D/VIX 1.0273 vs 0.9284 at p=0.0479, stable across five seeds (0.0474-0.0513) unlike February's near-miss -- but late-September sessions (day>=20) carry the same steepening in BOTH eras independently (2008-2020: 0.9742 vs 0.9447, p=0.0176; 2021+: 0.9908 vs 0.9309, p=0.0170), it is NOT a generic month-end effect (all day>=22 sessions 2021+, ratio p=0.1374), and against other late-September sessions the release lands at p=0.5334. THE CONTROL GRANULARITY IS THE TRANSFERABLE LESSON: a month-level control would have missed this, and FHFA's last-Tuesday rule puts EVERY release in the final third of its month, so the February and August ledgers used a systematically too-coarse control. Both verdicts survive re-testing at the sharper granularity (February p=0.61/0.58/0.85/0.89; August 0.52/0.54/0.61/0.79) -- the method is upgraded, the conclusions are not corrected. THE 2027 FED QUIRK CUTS THE OTHER WAY HERE. The Board posted September 2027 as Sep 14-15, the second Tuesday -- the break that cost the August sibling seven days of separation (21 -> 14). For September it BUYS seven: a third-Tuesday September would have put this print 6 days after the decision (the modal September value, 4 of 5 since 2021); the actual gap is 13, tied with 2025-09-30 for the widest a September FHFA release has had, and reached by a different mechanism (2025 got there on a five-Tuesday September). Not in a blackout: Sep 4-16 cleared by 12 days, Oct 16-28 by 18. CONTENT -- JULY IS THE FIFTH REFERENCE MONTH TESTED AND THE FIRST WEAK ONE: 12 of 14 positive since 2012, the WORST of the twelve (85.7%), 28 of 35 all-time, and the most recent July on record printed NEGATIVE (2025-07, -0.10%) -- yet still p=0.4331. Four perfect months and now the weakest month all fail to separate, which closes the seasonal hypothesis from both ends. A PARSING TRAP BANKED: the Board's 2027 FOMC panel footnote announces a 2028 meeting ("Note: A two-day meeting is scheduled for January 25-26, 2028."), so a year-scoped parse returns 57 meetings with a phantom 2027-01-25/26 and corrupts every nearest-FOMC-day figure; cutting each panel at its footnote restores 56, 8 per year. IMPACT STAYS low. symbols: [] and 0 hits for any housing or house-price keying in trade-playbooks.md or multi-symbol-sweep.md (re-grepped 2026-09-06); nothing here licenses an entry.
